label: rem:einstein-nonsymmetric-metric-comparison
title: Position against Einstein's non-symmetric field theory
html:
Einstein's non-symmetric field theory [einstein1925, einstein1946, einstein1955], pursued in parallel by Schrödinger [schrodinger1950], sought to unify gravitation and electromagnetism by discarding the symmetry of the metric:

  g_{\mu\nu}
  \;=\;
  g_{(\mu\nu)} + g_{[\mu\nu]},

with the symmetric part g_{(\mu\nu)} carrying gravitation and the antisymmetric part g_{[\mu\nu]} intended to carry the Maxwell field. The programme did not succeed: g_{[\mu\nu]} never reproduced Maxwell's equations, and its modern descendant, Moffat's nonsymmetric gravitational theory [moffat1995], carries linearisation instabilities and ghost modes in the antisymmetric sector [damour1993].

Position of the QOU construction. The QOU substrate carries a symmetric–antisymmetric decomposition with the same force assignment Einstein sought, but the decomposition is not carried by a metric. It is the eigenvalue decomposition of the braiding.

By the Hecke relation, the braiding c_{V,V} splits V \otimes V into \mathrm{Sym}^2_q(V) \oplus \Lambda^2_q(V) and acts on the two summands by the scalars q and -q^{-1}. Writing \lambda = \ln q, the two crossing energy weights resolve as

  q = \cosh\lambda + \sinh\lambda,
  \qquad -q^{-1} = -\cosh\lambda + \sinh\lambda.

Reversing a crossing negates its \cosh part and leaves its \sinh part unchanged. For a composite carrying p positive and m negative crossings the decomposition therefore reads

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}
  =
  (p - m)\cosh\lambda + (p + m)\sinh\lambda,

so the mirror operation \sigma, which exchanges p and m, negates the symmetric total and fixes the antisymmetric total. The \cosh channel binds independently of charge; the sign-blind \sinh channel distinguishes charge (channel identification), and is what survives when a composite is paired with its mirror. The electromagnetic coupling is a multiple of the antisymmetric eigenvalue q^{-1}.

Comparison.

Non-symmetric field theory QOU
Carrier of the decomposition metric g_{\mu\nu} on spacetime braiding c_{V,V} on \mathbf{C}
Symmetric part gravitation strong binding, \cosh\lambda
Antisymmetric part electromagnetism (intended) Coulomb interaction, \sinh\lambda
Origin of the decomposition postulated forced by the Hecke quadratic
Behaviour at q = 1 no analogue antisymmetric channel vanishes identically

Three structural differences.

  1. The QOU metric is symmetric and emergent. Gravitation in this framework is the geometry of the acoustic metric of the Madelung brane flow, which is symmetric. No antisymmetric part of a metric appears anywhere in the construction. The asymmetry is located upstream of spacetime, in the braided category; the metric is downstream and emergent.

  2. The instability results do not transfer. The inconsistency theorems of [damour1993] concern a propagating antisymmetric tensor field with its own field equations. The QOU antisymmetric channel is an eigenvalue of a braiding morphism in a rigid monoidal category and satisfies no field equations, so those results have no target here. The framework is correspondingly not a competing theory of non-symmetric gravitation; it is compared with the canonical quantum-gravity programmes in the preceding section, not with this one.

  3. The q-deformation of the metric is conformal, not antisymmetric. The parameter q does act on a metric in the contact deformation, interpolating the Levi-Civita connection to its Reeb projection. That deformation is conformal and contact-theoretic; it does not add an antisymmetric part.

Note on terminology. The torsion appearing in the substrate parameter axiom is the torsion subgroup \mu_\infty \subset \mathbb{G}_m of roots of unity, which the substrate section must avoid. It is unrelated to the torsion tensor of an affine connection used in Einstein--Cartan theory and in nonsymmetric gravitational theory.
